title: What is fermentation?
group: HOWN — How and Why in Nature
examples: Why does fermented food last longer?

explain.say: Fermentation is when microbes like yeast or bacteria feed on sugar without needing oxygen and turn it into something new. People have used it for thousands of years to make bread, yoghurt, cheese and pickles.
Yeast fermentation turns sugar into carbon dioxide gas and a little alcohol. The gas makes bread rise, and the bubbles in some drinks come from it too.
Lactic acid bacteria turn sugar into lactic acid instead. The acid gives yoghurt, sauerkraut and kimchi their sour tang, and it stops harmful microbes growing, so the food keeps longer.
Making yoghurt is a fermentation you can watch. Warm milk plus a spoonful of live yoghurt: the bacteria eat the milk sugar, make acid, and the acid makes the milk proteins set thick.

stages.note: Heated, then cooled to blood warmth

faq.q: Why does fermentation make food last longer?
faq.a: Fermenting microbes fill food with acid or alcohol and use up the sugar, which makes it hard for harmful microbes to grow. That is how people kept food long before fridges.

faq.q: Who discovered fermentation is caused by microbes?
faq.a: Louis Pasteur showed in the 1850s and 1860s that living microbes cause fermentation, and that different microbes make different products, such as alcohol or lactic acid.
Bread, yoghurt, cheese, sauerkraut, kimchi, soy sauce, miso, vinegar, chocolate and many pickles all rely on fermentation by yeasts, bacteria or moulds.

Milk is warmed and mixed with live bacteria, usually Lactobacillus bulgaricus and Streptococcus thermophilus. Kept warm for several hours, they turn milk sugar into lactic acid, which thickens the milk.
No. Fermentation is a way of getting energy from sugar without oxygen. That is why pickle jars and cheeses can keep fermenting even when sealed.

facts: Louis Pasteur showed in the 1850s that fermentation is carried out by living microbes.
Yoghurt is usually made with the bacteria Lactobacillus bulgaricus and Streptococcus thermophilus.
Cocoa beans are fermented for several days before they are dried and made into chocolate.
